Title: Cheesy Taco Taters (Loaded Veg) (Facebook Reel)

Items: 680 g potatoes, cut into 2–3 cm chunks (skin on or peeled)
130 ml water (about 1/3 of the tomato can)
1/2 tsp ground cumin (optional, if you want it more "taco")
150 g grated cheese (cheddar or Mexican-style blend)

Instructions: Heat 15 ml oil in a large frying pan with a lid over medium-high heat.

Add the 680 g potato chunks. Season with a good pinch of salt and sprinkle over 1/2 packet taco seasoning, plus 1/2 tsp smoked paprika and 1/2 tsp ground cumin (if using). Stir well so the potatoes are evenly coated.
Cook for 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are starting to soften on the edges but are not fully cooked yet.
Add the diced onion, diced red pepper, and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the onion softens and the mushrooms start to release their water.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Push the potato/veg mix to one side of the pan. Add 500 g beef mince to the empty side and season with salt and black pepper.
Cook the beef until browned, breaking it up with a spoon. Once cooked through, mix the beef into the potatoes and veg.
Add 1 x 400 g can diced tomatoes plus 130 ml water (about 1/3 of the tomato can). Stir everything together.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover the pan and turn the heat down to medium or medium-low.
Cook covered for about 10 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the potatoes are tender and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning (salt/pepper). If you want more punch, add a pinch more taco seasoning or a dash of chilli flakes.
Sprinkle 150 g grated cheese evenly over the top. Cover again and cook for 2–3 minutes (off the heat is fine) until the cheese is melted.
Serve hot with any toppings you like (sour cream, spring onions, coriander, jalapeños, hot sauce, lime).
Customizations: More heat: add 1/2 tsp cayenne or extra chilli flakes, or finish with chilli oil.
Herby finish: stir in chopped coriander at the end or garnish with parsley if you don’t like coriander.
Extra smoky: add another pinch of smoked paprika.
Add beans: stir in a drained can of black beans for extra bulk.
OptionalInstructions: If your potatoes are larger or your pan runs cool, you may need an extra 5 minutes covered—add a splash more water if it looks dry.
For a thicker, less saucy finish, uncover for the last 2–3 minutes before adding cheese so some liquid evaporates.
For crispier potatoes, use a wide pan and avoid overcrowding; stir less often in the first 5–7 minutes.
ServingSuggestions: Serve as-is, or with a side salad.
Great wrapped in tortillas as a quick taco/burrito filling.
Nice with a squeeze of lime and a dollop of sour cream.
